topics: Analysis of Clocked Synchronous Sequential Networks (CSSN)
State assignment problem and the transition table
Hazards – static and dynamic hazards in combinational networks
Practical issues- clock skew and jitter
Fault table method – path sensitization method – Boolean difference method
Automatic test pattern generation – Built in Self-Test (BIST)
VHDL constructs and codes for combinational and sequential circuits.

courseOutcomes.description: Design, analyze, and model clocked synchronous sequential networks (CSSNs), optimize state assignment and reduction, and effectively utilize ASM charts for the realization of complex digital systems.

Design and analyze asynchronous sequential circuits (ASCs), perform flow table reduction, address race conditions and state assignment problems, and design both ASCs and Arithmetic Logic Units (ALUs).
Identify and mitigate static and dynamic hazards in combinational networks, design hazard-free circuits, address practical issues in digital systems and apply fault detection and testing methods.
Explain the VLSI design flow, utilize various design entry methods, apply different VHDL modeling styles, and develop and simulate VHDL constructs for combinational and sequential circuits.
